description:
FOUND s438i (Opus 5), exposed by #450 the same way as #489 -- the pattern has
no wildcard, so before that fix it answered empty and the text was never seen.

  print glob(q(./"TEST")), "\n";
  # perl: ./TEST          PCL: ./"TEST"

perl's glob goes through File::Glob::csh_glob, which follows csh quoting rules:
a double- or single-quoted RUN inside the pattern is unquoted (and its contents
protected from splitting and from metacharacter interpretation).  t/op/glob.t
line 131 has the comment in so many words -- "Should we strip quotes in
Perl_vms_start_glob the way csh_glob() does?" -- so the stripping is csh_glob's
documented behaviour, not an accident.

RELATED, and the reason this is its own task: #450 gave PCL perl's WORD model
(a glob pattern is a whitespace-separated list), and csh quoting is the other
half of that model -- `glob('"a b"')` is ONE word in perl, not two.  Probe that
before implementing: the quote rules and the splitting rules have to land
together or the split will break quoted spaces.

FIX SHAPE: a csh-quoting pass in `%p-glob--split-words` (it already owns the
word model): walk the pattern, track single/double quote state, split only on
UNQUOTED whitespace, and drop the quote characters from the emitted word.
Perl's own edges to probe first: an UNBALANCED quote, a backslash-escaped
quote, and a quote inside a character class.

BAR: the probe above plus `glob('"a b"')`, `glob("'a b'")` and the unbalanced
case; a row in Pl/t/punct-array-glob-01.t beside #450's; `cl/` change, so the
full sweep plus the io/ and op/ companion dirs.
subject: glob does not strip QUOTES the way csh_glob does: `glob(q(./"TEST"))` keeps the double quotes where perl returns ./TEST
